questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the tools of genetic engineering:
1. Restriction endonucleases cut DNA at specific recognition sequences, many of which are palindromic.
2. DNA ligase joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds.
3. Taq polymerase used in PCR is obtained from the heat-loving bacterium Thermus aquaticus.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. Taq polymerase survives the roughly 95 degree Celsius denaturation step, so fresh enzyme need not be added in every PCR cycle, and ligase seals the fragments that restriction enzymes have cut.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Biotechnology: Principles and Processes
questions.h: Scissors (restriction enzyme), glue (ligase), photocopier (Taq in PCR)

questions.q:
With reference to CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing, consider the following statements:
1. It was adapted from a defence mechanism used by bacteria against viruses.
2. A guide RNA directs the Cas9 enzyme to the target DNA sequence.
3. Cas9 itself joins the cut DNA ends by acting as a ligase.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Cas9 is a nuclease that makes a double-strand cut where the guide RNA matches; it does not join the ends. The cell's own repair machinery then mends the break, which is how edits are introduced.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Biotechnology and its Applications; PIB explainers on genome editing

questions.q: The 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna for the development of:
questions.e: They showed that CRISPR-Cas9 can be programmed with a guide RNA to cut DNA at a chosen site, popularly called genetic scissors. PCR (Mullis), Sanger sequencing and hybridoma technology (Kohler and Milstein) won earlier Nobel Prizes.
questions.s: Nobel Prize official announcement, 2020

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Bt cotton:
1. It carries a gene from Bacillus thuringiensis that codes for a crystal (Cry) protein toxic to certain insect larvae.
2. The toxin becomes active in the alkaline conditions of the insect gut.
3. In India, the Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change decides on its environmental release.
4. It protects the crop from sucking pests such as aphids and whiteflies.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 to 3 are correct. Bt toxins target lepidopteran caterpillars such as bollworms; sucking pests such as aphids and whiteflies are not affected, which is why farmers still spray against them.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Biotechnology and its Applications; GEAC (MoEFCC)

questions.q: Golden Rice has been genetically engineered to produce:
o: beta-carotene, a precursor of vitamin A
an iron-binding protein to fight anaemia
questions.e: Golden Rice was developed to tackle vitamin A deficiency, and the beta-carotene gives the grain its yellow colour. It does not add vitamin B12, iron or lysine.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Biotechnology and its Applications

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about GM mustard hybrid DMH-11:
1. It was developed by a team at the University of Delhi using the barnase-barstar system for hybrid seed production.
2. It also carries the bar gene that makes the plant tolerant to a herbicide.
3. It has been under commercial cultivation across northern India since 2010.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Barnase causes male sterility, barstar restores fertility and bar gives herbicide tolerance. GEAC recommended environmental release in 2022, but it is not under commercial cultivation, as the matter went to the Supreme Court.
questions.s: GEAC; The Hindu, Oct 2022

questions.q: In February 2010, the Union Government imposed a moratorium on the commercial release of which genetically modified crop?
questions.e: After public consultations, the Environment Minister of the time put the GEAC-cleared Bt brinjal on hold pending further studies. Bt cotton, approved in 2002, remains the commercialised GM crop.
questions.s: GEAC / MoEFCC statement, Feb 2010

questions.q:
Statement-I: Under the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety, an importing country may restrict the import of a living modified organism even when scientific evidence of harm is not complete.
Statement-II: The Protocol incorporates the precautionary approach.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Protocol, adopted in 2000 under the Convention on Biological Diversity, allows such decisions because it is built on the precautionary approach. Hence Statement-II is the reason for Statement-I.
questions.s: CBD Secretariat; Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Cartagena Protocol : Safe handling and transboundary movement of living modified organisms
2. Nagoya Protocol : Access to genetic resources and fair sharing of benefits
3. Nagoya-Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocol : Access and benefit sharing of genetic resources
4. Rotterdam Convention : Trade in hazardous wastes
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. The Nagoya-Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocol deals with liability and redress for damage from living modified organisms, and the Rotterdam Convention deals with prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals and pesticides, while hazardous wastes come under the Basel Convention.
questions.s: CBD Secretariat; Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 1989 rules on hazardous microorganisms and genetically engineered organisms are notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
2. The Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee functions under the Department of Biotechnology.
3. The Review Committee on Genetic Manipulation functions under the Department of Biotechnology.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The GEAC is the apex body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change that approves large-scale use and environmental release. The RCGM sits in the DBT and reviews research-level biosafety data.
questions.s: MoEFCC / DBT biosafety framework; Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about genome-edited plants in India:
1. SDN-1 creates a small random change at the target site through the cell's own repair, without any repair template.
2. SDN-2 uses a small repair template to bring about a specific small change.
3. SDN-3 involves insertion of a larger DNA sequence, often a foreign gene, and is not exempted from GM regulation.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The 2022 MoEFCC order exempted SDN-1 and SDN-2 plants that carry no foreign DNA from the stringent GM rules, because their products resemble conventional mutations, while SDN-3 stays under GM rules.
questions.s: MoEFCC order, March 2022
questions.h: 1 = Snip, 2 = Swap, 3 = Stitch in new gene

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes the two genome-edited rice varieties, DRR Dhan 100 (Kamala) and Pusa DST Rice 1, released in India in 2025?
o: They are transgenic varieties containing the Bt gene from Bacillus thuringiensis
They are hybrids produced using the barnase-barstar male sterility system
They were developed by ICAR institutes using site-directed nuclease genome editing without inserting foreign DNA
They were produced by exposing seeds to gamma radiation (mutation breeding)
questions.e: These varieties came from ICAR institutes and were edited in endogenous genes (SDN-1 type), so they carry no foreign DNA and were handled under the 2022 genome-editing guidelines. They are therefore not transgenic like Bt crops.
questions.s: PIB, May 2025

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about stem cells:
1. The zygote is totipotent.
2. Embryonic stem cells are pluripotent.
3. Adult stem cells such as haematopoietic stem cells are pluripotent and can form any cell type of the body.
4. Embryonic stem cells can differentiate into extra-embryonic tissues such as the placenta in addition to all body cells.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only 1 and 2 are correct. Adult stem cells are generally multipotent, restricted to a related set of cell types, and pluripotent embryonic stem cells form body cells but not the placenta, which is why only the zygote is totipotent.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Biology, Cell Cycle; ICMR-DBT Stem Cell Guidelines
questions.h: Toti = Total, Pluri = Plenty, Multi = Many (few)

questions.q:
Statement-I: Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) were introduced as a way around the ethical objections to using human embryos.
Statement-II: iPSCs were first obtained in 2006 by Shinya Yamanaka by reprogramming mouse skin fibroblasts.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are true. iPSCs are made from adult body cells with a few reprogramming factors, so no embryo is destroyed, but the 2006 first derivation in mice does not itself explain the ethical advantage.
questions.s: Nobel Prize 2012 (Medicine) announcement

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding stem cell research in India:
1. The ICMR and the Department of Biotechnology issued National Guidelines for Stem Cell Research in 2017, which prohibit reproductive cloning of humans.
2. Stem cell therapies may be freely sold commercially for any disease.
3. Stem cell derived products are regulated as new drugs under the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Outside bone marrow type haematopoietic transplantation for blood disorders, stem cell uses remain investigational and are allowed only within approved clinical trials, so free commercial sale is wrong.
questions.s: ICMR-DBT National Guidelines for Stem Cell Research, 2017; NDCT Rules 2019

questions.q: Dolly, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell in 1996, was produced by:
o: somatic cell nuclear transfer, placing the nucleus of an udder cell into an enucleated egg
splitting an early embryo into two halves
fusing two eggs from different sheep and activating them without sperm
in vitro fertilisation followed by insertion of a growth hormone gene
questions.e: The nucleus from a mammary (udder) cell was put into an egg whose own nucleus had been removed, and the egg was then stimulated to divide. It proved that a specialised adult nucleus can be reprogrammed to direct development.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology; Roslin Institute, 1996

questions.q:
Match List-I (COVID-19 vaccine used in India) with List-II (platform):
A. Covaxin
B. Covishield
C. Corbevax
D. ZyCoV-D
1. Recombinant protein sub-unit
2. Chimpanzee adenovirus vector
3. Plasmid DNA
4. Inactivated whole virus
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Covaxin uses inactivated whole virus, Covishield (ChAdOx1) a chimpanzee adenovirus vector, Corbevax the spike protein receptor-binding domain, and ZyCoV-D a plasmid DNA. Mixing up the vector and inactivated types is the common slip.
questions.s: PIB / ICMR vaccine fact sheets, 2021-22

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. mRNA vaccines deliver instructions that are read in the cytoplasm and do not enter the nucleus to change the host DNA.
2. After vaccination, mRNA is converted into DNA by reverse transcriptase and integrates into the human chromosomes.
3. The 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for nucleoside base modifications that made mRNA vaccines effective.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: mRNA is translated by ribosomes and degrades soon after, and vaccine mRNA has no mechanism that routinely writes it into the genome. Katalin Kariko and Drew Weissman won the 2023 prize for the base modifications that reduced inflammatory reaction.
questions.s: Nobel Prize 2023 (Medicine) announcement

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about vaccines:
1. BCG is a live attenuated vaccine.
2. The oral polio vaccine contains live attenuated virus, while the injectable polio vaccine contains inactivated virus.
3. Tetanus vaccine is made from an inactivated toxin (toxoid).
4. The hepatitis B vaccine is a recombinant protein vaccine prepared by expressing the surface antigen in yeast.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. Live attenuated vaccines mimic infection, toxoids train the body against the toxin rather than the bacterium, and recombinant hepatitis B surface antigen was among the first vaccines made by genetic engineering.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Human Health and Disease; WHO fact sheets

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly matches the generation of biofuel with its feedstock?
o: First generation : algae grown in ponds
Second generation : lignocellulosic residues such as rice straw
Second generation : edible oilseeds such as soybean
questions.e: Second generation biofuels use non-food biomass such as straw, bagasse and wood waste, avoiding the food versus fuel conflict. First generation uses food crops, and third generation uses algae.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Energy; PIB on biofuels

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about biofuel policy in India:
1. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas is the nodal ministry for the National Policy on Biofuels, 2018.
2. The 2018 policy bans the use of any food grain for ethanol production under all circumstances.
3. A 2022 amendment advanced the target of 20 per cent ethanol blending in petrol to 2025-26 from 2030.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The policy permits surplus food grains for ethanol with approval of the National Biofuel Coordination Committee when there is a surplus, in addition to sugarcane juice, molasses and damaged grains.
questions.s: PIB, 2018 and May 2022

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. SATAT : Promotes production of ethanol from sugarcane juice
2. GOBARdhan : Converts cattle dung and organic waste into biogas and compost
3. PM JI-VAN Yojana : Gives financial support for Jatropha based biodiesel
4. Global Biofuels Alliance : Launched during the G20 Summit in New Delhi in 2023
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 2 and 4 are correct. SATAT promotes compressed biogas as automotive fuel, and PM JI-VAN Yojana supports second generation (lignocellulosic) ethanol projects, not Jatropha biodiesel.
questions.s: PIB; MoPNG

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Biodiesel is produced by transesterification of vegetable oils or animal fats, with glycerol as a by-product.
2. Biodiesel is chemically identical to petroleum diesel, being a mixture of hydrocarbons.
3. Bioethanol is produced mainly by anaerobic digestion of cattle dung by methanogens.
4. Pongamia and Jatropha oils are edible oils preferred for biodiesel because of their taste.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only the first is correct. Biodiesel consists of fatty acid methyl esters, not hydrocarbons, bioethanol comes from yeast fermentation of sugars (anaerobic digestion gives biogas), and Jatropha and Pongamia are non-edible oils.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Energy; NCERT Class XII Chemistry

questions.q: In bioinformatics, which one of the following tools is used to compare a DNA or protein sequence against databases to find regions of similarity?
questions.e: BLAST (Basic Local Alignment Search Tool) of the NCBI aligns a query sequence against stored sequences. The others are laboratory techniques, not software.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Biotechnology and its Applications

questions.q: The 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry recognised work on:
o: computational protein design and prediction of protein structure from amino acid sequence
questions.e: David Baker was recognised for computational protein design, and Demis Hassabis and John Jumper for AlphaFold, which predicts a protein's 3D structure from its sequence. CRISPR won in 2020, quantum dots in 2023 and click chemistry in 2022.
questions.s: Nobel Prize 2024 (Chemistry) announcement

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. INSACOG was set up to track variants of the SARS-CoV-2 virus through genome sequencing.
2. The Indian Biological Data Centre at Faridabad, under the Department of Biotechnology, is India's first national repository for life science data.
3. The Indian Biological Data Centre is run by the Indian Council of Medical Research.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: INSACOG was a consortium of laboratories formed in late 2020. The IBDC is hosted at the Regional Centre for Biotechnology, Faridabad, an institution of the Department of Biotechnology, and not the ICMR.
questions.s: PIB, 2020 and DBT press release, 2022

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Human Genome Project:
1. It was declared complete in 2003.
2. Less than 2 per cent of the human genome codes for proteins.
3. It showed that humans have the largest number of genes among all organisms.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The project revealed that most of the genome is non-coding, and humans have far fewer genes than expected, so the idea that humans have the most genes is wrong. Bioinformatics was central to storing and analysing the sequence.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.q: DNA fingerprinting, developed by Alec Jeffreys, is based on differences among individuals in:
o: the sequence of exons that code for haemoglobin
the promoter regions of housekeeping genes
the number of chromosomes in somatic cells
the number of tandem repeats in variable number tandem repeat (VNTR) regions
questions.e: VNTRs are repeated short sequences whose copy number differs between persons, giving a unique banding pattern, inherited from both parents. The coding exons of common genes are largely alike, and chromosome number is the same in all humans.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.q: What is the correct order of steps in one cycle of the polymerase chain reaction (PCR)?
o: Annealing of primers, denaturation of DNA, extension by Taq polymerase
Extension by Taq polymerase, denaturation of DNA, annealing of primers
Denaturation of DNA, annealing of primers, extension by Taq polymerase
Denaturation of DNA, extension by Taq polymerase, annealing of primers
questions.e: Heat first separates the strands, cooling lets primers bind, and then the polymerase extends from the primers. Extension cannot begin before the primers are annealed.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Biotechnology: Principles and Processes

questions.q:
Statement-I: Taq polymerase can be used directly to amplify the RNA genome of a virus in a PCR without any prior step.
Statement-II: Taq polymerase is a DNA-dependent DNA polymerase.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Taq copies only DNA templates, so RNA viruses such as SARS-CoV-2 must first be converted to complementary DNA by reverse transcriptase, which is the RT in RT-PCR. Statement-I is therefore incorrect and Statement-II is correct.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Biotechnology: Principles and Processes

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about monoclonal antibodies:
1. A monoclonal antibody is produced by a single clone of antibody-producing cells and recognises a single epitope.
2. Hybridoma cells are formed by fusing an antibody-producing B lymphocyte with a myeloma cell.
3. The hybridoma technique was developed by Kary Mullis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Hybridomas combine the specificity of the B cell with the unlimited growth of the cancer cell. The technique is from Kohler and Milstein, and Kary Mullis is known for PCR.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Human Health and Disease

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about recombinant human insulin:
1. Mature human insulin has two polypeptide chains, A and B, linked by disulphide bridges.
2. In humans, insulin is made as a pro-hormone, and the C peptide is removed during maturation.
3. The first recombinant human insulin, produced in 1982, used Agrobacterium tumefaciens as the host.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The first rDNA insulin was made by Eli Lilly in Escherichia coli, with chains A and B produced separately and then joined. Agrobacterium is used for plant transformation, not for making insulin.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Biotechnology and its Applications

questions.q: Which one of the following is commonly used as a natural vector to introduce genes into dicot plants?
o: Rhizobium leguminosarum, using its nod genes
Agrobacterium tumefaciens, using its Ti plasmid
questions.e: Agrobacterium naturally transfers a part of its Ti plasmid (T-DNA) into plant cells, and scientists replace the tumour-causing genes with the desired gene. For cereals, which are monocots, the gene gun is often used.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Biotechnology: Principles and Processes

questions.q: Nematode-resistant tobacco was developed using which one of the following approaches?
o: Insertion of the Bt cry gene for a crystal protein
Terminator technology to make nematodes sterile
Somatic hybridisation with a nematode-resistant relative
RNA interference, in which complementary double-stranded RNA silences a nematode gene
questions.e: A vector carrying sense and antisense RNA of a nematode gene made double-stranded RNA in the host, which silenced the nematode's mRNA and halted its growth in roots. Bt toxins target insects, not nematodes.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Biotechnology and its Applications

questions.q:
Statement-I: A gene drive can spread an engineered trait through a population faster than ordinary Mendelian inheritance would allow.
Statement-II: Gene drives have been proposed as a way of controlling disease-carrying mosquitoes such as the malaria vector.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: A gene drive biases inheritance so that more than half of the offspring carry the trait. Mosquito control is only one proposed application, and it does not explain how the drive works.
questions.s: Science and Technology, current affairs compilations

questions.q:
Statement-I: Plants regenerated from shoot-tip meristem culture are often free of viruses, even when the mother plant is infected.
Statement-II: The apical meristem has actively dividing cells and little or no developed vascular tissue, so viruses seldom reach it.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Viruses spread within a plant mainly through the vascular system, which is absent in the meristem tip, so the tip stays clean. This is why meristem culture is used to obtain virus-free planting material.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production

questions.q: The first living organism to be granted a patent in the United States, after a landmark 1980 Supreme Court decision, was:
o: a genetically engineered Pseudomonas bacterium capable of degrading components of crude oil
questions.e: Ananda Chakrabarty's bacterium was held to be a human-made invention rather than a product of nature. This case opened the way for patenting of microorganisms and is often cited in debates on patents over life forms.
questions.s: Diamond v. Chakrabarty (US Supreme Court, 1980)

questions.q: Which genetically modified food, approved for sale in the United States in 1994, was engineered for delayed ripening through reduced activity of a pectin-degrading enzyme?
questions.e: By lowering polygalacturonase, the tomato stayed firm longer, and it is regarded as the first commercially available GM food crop. Golden Rice and Bt brinjal are not marketed on this basis.
questions.s: Standard biotechnology references

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sickle cell disease is caused by a point mutation in the beta-globin gene that replaces glutamic acid with valine.
2. The first CRISPR-based therapy to receive regulatory approval, in 2023, was for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassaemia.
3. Sickle cell disease is an X-linked dominant disorder.
4. The National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission, launched in 2023, aims at elimination by 2030.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Sickle cell disease is autosomal recessive, and the mission launched in 2023 targets elimination as a public health problem by 2047.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Principles of Inheritance; PIB, July 2023

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about CAR-T cell therapy:
1. The patient's own T cells are modified to carry a chimeric antigen receptor that recognises cancer cells.
2. NexCAR19, approved in India in 2023, targets the CD19 protein on certain B-cell cancers.
3. It is a preventive vaccine given to healthy people against cancer-causing viruses.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: CAR-T therapy is a personalised treatment given to cancer patients, not a preventive vaccine. NexCAR19 was developed by ImmunoACT, linked to IIT Bombay and Tata Memorial Centre.
questions.s: PIB, 2024; CDSCO approval, Oct 2023

questions.q: The first clinical gene therapy, carried out in 1990, was for the treatment of:
questions.e: A girl with ADA deficiency, which cripples the immune system, received her own lymphocytes carrying a functional ADA gene. Gene therapy for the other disorders followed much later.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Biotechnology and its Applications

questions.q: Which one of the following transgenic cows produced milk enriched with the human protein alpha-lactalbumin?
questions.e: Rosie, born in 1997, produced milk with a protein more balanced for human infants. Dolly was a cloned sheep, and Garima and Samrupa were cloned buffalo calves from India, not transgenic cows.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Biotechnology and its Applications

questions.q: Which one of the following is a free-living, nitrogen-fixing bacterium used as a biofertiliser?
questions.e: Azotobacter fixes nitrogen without a host plant. Rhizobium fixes nitrogen only in legume root nodules, Glomus is a mycorrhizal fungus that helps phosphorus uptake, and Nitrosomonas is a nitrifying bacterium that oxidises ammonia.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Microbes in Human Welfare

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Biological Weapons Convention prohibits the development, production and stockpiling of biological and toxin weapons.
Statement-II: The Convention has a formal verification and inspection body like the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The BWC, in force since 1975, bans such weapons, but unlike the Chemical Weapons Convention it has no standing inspectorate, which is a long-standing criticism of its design.
questions.s: UNODA; Defence and security compilations

questions.q: In the four-level classification of laboratory biosafety, BSL-4 laboratories are meant for work with:
o: non-disease-causing strains of Escherichia coli used in teaching
common bacteria such as Staphylococcus aureus
dangerous exotic agents such as Ebola and Marburg viruses
questions.e: BSL-4 is the highest containment level, with full-body positive-pressure suits. Teaching strains fall under BSL-1, common pathogens under BSL-2, and tuberculosis or coronavirus cultures under BSL-3.
questions.s: WHO Laboratory Biosafety Manual; ICMR

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about biological control:
1. Trichoderma species are fungi used to protect plants against soil-borne pathogens.
2. Baculoviruses of the genus Nucleopolyhedrovirus are used against insect pests and are species-specific.
3. Bacillus thuringiensis spores are formulated as bioinsecticides against caterpillars.
4. Biocontrol agents are broad-spectrum and kill all insects, including beneficial ones.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Biocontrol agents are chosen because they are narrow in their action, with little harm to beneficial insects or non-target organisms. The fourth statement therefore reverses the main advantage of these agents.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Microbes in Human Welfare

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Department of Biotechnology functions under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
2. BIRAC is a not-for-profit public sector company set up by the Department of Biotechnology to support biotechnology start-ups and innovation.
3. The BioE3 Policy (Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment) was approved by the Union Cabinet in 2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: DBT is part of the Ministry of Science and Technology, not the Health Ministry. BIRAC, set up in 2012, and the 2024 BioE3 policy together aim to scale up biomanufacturing and bio-startups.
questions.s: PIB, Aug 2024; BIRAC

questions.q: Terminator technology, a controversial application of genetic engineering, refers to:
o: engineering plants to resist a particular herbicide
engineering plants to delay fruit ripening
engineering pests to die after a single generation
engineering plants to produce sterile seeds so that farmers cannot replant them
questions.e: Genetic use restriction technology prevents seeds from germinating in the next season, forcing farmers to buy fresh seed. Concern over it is linked to the farmers' right to save seed.
questions.s: Standard biotechnology and IPR references

questions.q:
Arrange the following milestones in chronological order:
1. Birth of Dolly, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell
2. Construction of the first recombinant DNA molecule
3. Declaration of completion of the Human Genome Project
4. Publication of CRISPR-Cas9 as a programmable genome editing tool
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Recombinant DNA came in 1973, Dolly in 1996, the genome project in 2003 and the programmable CRISPR-Cas9 tool in 2012. The 2012 date is what separates the last two options.
questions.s: Standard biotechnology references

questions.q: The cryIAb gene of Bacillus thuringiensis, used in genetically modified crops, provides protection against which pest?
questions.e: cryIAb is used against the corn borer, while cryIAc and cryIIAb control cotton bollworms. Nematodes are handled by RNA interference, not Cry toxins.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Biotechnology and its Applications
